chunks: 33 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
He who says: 'There is no god but Allah' one hundred times will be the best of the people in deeds on that day, unless someone says it more often than he does.

key_terms.أَفْضَلَ النَّاسِ: The best/most excellent of the people
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (The declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting 'La ilaha illallah' 100 times daily?
ai.summary: In *Al-Tawhid*, Shaykh al-Saduq cites this chain to emphasize the spiritual supremacy of *Tahlil* (La ilaha illa Allah) as a foundational act of worship. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of simple, sincere monotheistic declaration, positioning it as a daily benchmark for excellence in deeds, provided no one surpasses it in volume or depth of understanding.
